bullets.title: Hot August CPI (+0.29% m/m) locks in 85-90% Fed hike odds for Sept 16 FOMC
bullets.body: August core CPI printed 0.29% m/m versus 0.2% consensus, with supercore services +0.51% m/m (highest since January) and wireless services +5.9% contributing 8-10 bps. Markets priced ~85-90% probability of a 25bp September hike, with 2-year yields rising 26bps on the week to 4.63% and 10-year yields approaching 4.97%—the highest since October 2023. Wolfe and 22V both expect hikes at September and December FOMCs, then a prolonged hold.

bullets.title: Inflation structurally sticky: nominal GDP +6.6%, M2 +7%, real rents re-accelerating
bullets.body: Core PCE tracked at ~0.22-0.25% m/m for August despite the headline CPI beat, but PSC Macro and 22V flag that accommodative conditions (fed funds 300bp below nominal GDP, M2 growing 7% annualized, bank loans +7%) make disinflation fragile. Hedgeye's nowcast targets September CPI at 3.54% (+14bp acceleration) and Q4 headline at 3.76%. Real-world rents are picking back up, suggesting CPI rent/OER reacceleration in 2027.

bullets.title: Bond yields approach critical resistance: 30-year bear exhaustion, 10-year at 2023 highs
bullets.body: The 10-year yield hit 4.97%, within a basis point of the October 2023 bear-cycle high, while the 30-year reversed from the 5.38-5.59% support zone showing potential bearish trend exhaustion. JPMorgan's technical team recommends entering a 25% initial long 30-year bond at market (5.45% stop), flagging T-note Daily Sentiment Index below 10% for the first time since 2022. 22V and Hedgeye both target 10-year yields toward 5-6% before any mean reversion.

bullets.title: Oil above $100/bbl on Iran/Houthi escalation; diesel at all-time highs create stagflationary risk
bullets.body: Brent crude traded as high as $108 intraweek before pulling back on reports of Gulf-Iran talks; WTI finished around $99. Houthis seized the port of Mokha near Bab al-Mandeb while Saudi oil production fell 1.9 mmbbl/d to 6.2 mmbbl/d—its lowest since 1990. US diesel topped $6/gallon for the first time on record. Wolfe DC Policy sees no quick diplomatic exit, with 'muddle forward' equilibrium as base case. JPMorgan's energy shock monitor shows US gas/diesel inventories at post-conflict lows.

bullets.title: ECB hikes 25bp to 2.50%; BoJ on track for 25bp hike next week; global tightening cycle broadens
bullets.body: The ECB raised rates as expected and signaled further work needed, with JPM expecting a final December hike (October live on upside inflation risk). The BoJ is universally expected to hike to 1.25% at the September meeting, with markets pricing ~1.75% policy rate sooner than prior forecasts. Euro area Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.6% annualized, but ex-Ireland only 1.2%. UK GDP surprised at +0.4% in July, pushing JPM's 3Q forecast to 2.0% annualized.

bullets.title: S&P 500 down 0.8% on week; IWM -2.4%, breadth collapses to 4:1 negative; small caps bearish trend
bullets.body: The S&P 500 snapped a two-week winning streak with the equal-weight index underperforming cap-weight by ~109bp. IWM broke its bearish trade and trend; 80%+ of S&P constituents were down on multiple sessions. Energy (+2%) and Communication Services (+1.2%) were the only positive sectors; Healthcare (-3.6%), Materials (-2.7%), and Cyclicals (-2.5%) led losses. Hedge fund net leverage retreated to 52% (25th percentile) with shorts outpacing longs 2:1.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle intact: MSFT triples datacenter to 38GW by 2032; OpenAI Astra rationing subs
bullets.body: Microsoft announced plans to add 26GW of compute capacity to reach 38GW total by 2032, with AI-specific capacity growing to ~13GW (one-third of total). OpenAI paused new $200/month ChatGPT Pro subscriptions citing 'unprecedented' Astra demand. NVIDIA's CEO reiterated 70% revenue growth for 2027. ORCL delivered 120% OCI growth with $30B+ in new AI bookings and 850MW of capacity delivered. JPM sees hyperscaler capex growing ~30% YoY and estimates AMZN AWS could hit 50%+ growth in 2027.

bullets.title: Compute market tightening: GPU contracts renewing at 20% premiums; neocloud pricing power validated
bullets.body: ORCL's older-generation GPU renewal contracts showed average 20% pricing premiums. 22V estimates CRWV consensus underprices compute at $12M/MW vs. $15-20M actual realizations on its 5.5GW open portfolio, with each $1M/MW improvement worth $17/share. IREN validated $25M/MW for 3-year deals and $40M/MW for sub-1-year. SPCX disclosed a new $13B ARR compute deal starting December. The FCF inflection for ORCL is expected 1-2 years out as major capex peaks.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure power/data center buildout faces political resistance and regulatory pushback
bullets.body: Wells Fargo flagged data center moratorium activity intensifying as a key November election issue. Multiple states (Ohio, Massachusetts, Charlotte NC) are canceling or pausing data center tax exemptions and permits. A Roth Capital survey is quantifying consumer blame attribution to AI data centers for rising electricity bills in PJM and ERCOT regions. MS notes that post-election conclusion in November should reduce adverse attention on data center development.

bullets.title: TMT/AI long buying at 7-month high; largest 2-week TMT buy since June '25 (97th percentile)
bullets.body: GS Prime shows TMT (Info Tech + Comm Svcs) as the most bought sector in 7 months in dollar terms. Separately, Goldman's weekly equity rundown flagged the largest 2-week long buying in TMT since June 2025 at the 97th percentile of the 5-year range. Hedge funds ended the week as net sellers overall but concentrated re-grossing was in high-quality tech and hyperscalers. Systematic strategies (Vol Target, CTA, Risk Parity) are fully positioned at the 81st percentile and could sell $12bn if SPX rallies 1%.

bullets.title: Consumer sentiment plunges to second-lowest on record; UMich at 47.8 vs 52.5 consensus
bullets.body: September University of Michigan consumer sentiment fell 7.5% to 47.8, the second-lowest reading on record. Year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.6% vs. 4.0% consensus. Healthcare premium inflation accelerated to 7.1% YoY in August as employers shift costs to workers. JPM's August consumer spending data showed acceleration to +5.1% YoY (discretionary +5.4%), but a $20B wallet headwind from gas prices is expected Sept-Dec.

bullets.title: FOMC, BoE, BoJ all meeting next week—the most consequential week of the macro calendar
bullets.body: The September 16 FOMC decision carries ~85-90% hike probability priced; the BoJ is expected to hike 25bp to 1.25% (most major banks unanimous); the BoE is expected to hold at 3.75% with a 6-3 vote but is seen shifting language hawkishly toward a November hike as August CPI is expected to print 3.2% YoY vs the BoE's 2.8% forecast. JPM expects QT pace to slow from £70bn to £50bn annually starting October.

bullets.title: Real estate/REITs underperform as 10-year yields spike 19bps on week to 4.97%
bullets.body: The S&P 500 RE Index fell 1.10% vs the broader market's -0.80% as mortgage rates hit 7.12%—the highest in over a year. Office REITs fell 3.39% and retail 2.12%. Existing home sales missed consensus with the highest inventory since late 2019 (1.62M units, 4.9 months supply). Hedgeye and Bloomberg data confirm rate-sensitive shorts are being covered while housing stocks remain in bearish trend.

bullets.title: Taiwan tech August sales +9% MoM/+69% YoY; hyperscaler capex revised up to +95% YoY in 2026
bullets.body: UBS reports Taiwan tech August sales well above the +1% 5-year seasonal baseline. Hyperscaler cloud capex was revised up to +95%/+43% YoY for 2026/2027 post-Oracle results. Memory prices are surging: Nanya Tech +561% YoY in August. Supply chain expected to remain tight through new platform ramps (Vera Rubin/Helios/TPU v8 starting Q4 2026). UBS prefers foundry (TSMC), back-end (ASE), fabless (Mediatek), and equipment suppliers with tight supply.

bullets.title: US-Iran 'forever conflict' base case; Hormuz talks offer potential off-ramp but military miscalculation risk elevated
bullets.body: Wolfe DC Policy sees the US-Iran standoff as entering a 'muddle forward' equilibrium: no clear military end-state, no diplomatic off-ramp without US sanctions relief, Iran pain intensifying but neither side willing to capitulate. Jefferies-X highlights that even a political settlement may not restore physical energy market normalcy—shipping insurance, freight adaptation, and product scarcity could persist. Goldman warns of $120/barrel oil risk if attacks intensify.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi meeting Sept 24; trade truce expires Nov 1; investors watching for tech controls, Taiwan, capital flows
bullets.body: Jefferies is hosting a preview call for the September 24 Trump-Xi summit. Key focus areas: trade, technology controls, Taiwan, capital flows, and supply chains. The existing trade truce agreement expires November 1, and copper tariffs appear to be stalling amid affordability concerns at the White House. Separately, Japan's PM Takaichi unveiled a ¥370tn investment roadmap targeting 17 strategic sectors.

bullets.title: AI tech inflation: DRAM +280% YoY, memory component prices lifting global core CPI by +0.2pp
bullets.body: An analysis from Morgan Stanley/JPM International notes that global tech CPI inflation swung from a -0.1pp drag in 2024-25 to a +0.1pp boost now, expected to reach +0.2pp by 1H27. DRAM prices are up 280% over the past year; equity analysts expect another 33% gain through mid-2027. NAND is expected to rise 21% further. US PCE tech inflation hit 15% 3m/3m SAAR in July vs CPI at 1%, with flash memory miscategorization accounting for much of the gap.

bullets.title: Equity risk premium compressed to 2.1%—lowest since 2002—raising rate sensitivity
bullets.body: JPMorgan flows research flags that the S&P 500 equity risk premium has declined to 2.1%, 100bp below historical averages and the lowest level since 2002. This increases equity sensitivity to bond yields, creates incentives to rebalance from equities to bonds, and reinforces positive bond-equity correlation. Non-bank investors are the most overweight equities vs. bonds since 2002. JPM remains Tactically Cautious/Neutral on global equities.

bullets.title: Sector rotation: Energy (+2%), Comm Services (+1.2%) win; Healthcare (-3.6%), Homebuilders, Restaurants sold
bullets.body: JPM flow data shows CTA crude oil positioning at the 85th LT percentile after being neutral in early July. Airlines reversed to selling (L/S at 3rd percentile). Homebuilders net sold with L/S ratio at the 5th percentile (first time since 2018). Restaurants net sold -1.7z over 20 days (L/S at 5th percentile LT). EU Energy switched to buying at the 90th percentile LT. Rate-sensitive sectors (Utilities, Housing, Industrials) continue to lag.

bullets.title: AI building from hardware to software/services: agentic AI monetization tangible at Communacopia and Citi TMT
bullets.body: The Goldman Communacopia and Citi TMT conferences both pointed to AI monetization becoming tangible: consumption/credit-based pricing is standard, SaaS systems-of-record are retaining pricing, and security is a clear winner via the 'Mythos effect.' NOW, CRM (Agentforce ARR $1.5B), CRWD, and CRWV emerged as standouts. Wolfe TMT conference highlighted security as the clearest beneficiary and agentic chip design (Cadence customers scaling from 10 to ~500 agents in one month) as a new theme.
